correctness.rationale: For a finite-dimensional real centrally symmetric polytope, its norm additivity ∥u+v∥=2 occurs exactly when u,v lie on a common exposed facet. Every vertex can be uniquely exposed by a norm-one functional and every relative-interior facet point belongs to exactly its facet. Sufficiency: choose a norming vertex of f and an orbit facet containing both that vertex and gy; a common supporting functional gives ∥v+tgy∥=1+t for arbitrary t=∥T∥>0. Necessity: if a vertex misses the orbit of a facet, the rank-one f⊗y with f uniquely exposing v and y in relint(F) cannot satisfy norm 2 for any g; compactness and equality in triangle inequality force x=±v, yielding contradiction. The action of the isometry group is faithful on the vertices, hence finite. For a regular even N-gon, each subgroup acts on facets by step-L translations and optionally j↦s−j; every pair of adjacent facet residues meets all orbits iff L≤2. Cases L=3,4,≥5 exclude all reflective and nonreflective subgroups, proving R² membership exactly. Isometry group is dihedral (can prove orthogonality from the second moment matrix of regular polygon vertices). This argument treats t>0, N=4, arbitrary even N, and arbitrary real polyhedral dimensions without relying on finite extrapolation.
residual_risks: Finite numerical diagnostics do not prove the universal classification; the analytic supporting-facet and residue-orbit arguments supply that proof.
No assertion about complex scalars, nonpolyhedral balls, or infinite-dimensional isometry actions.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for the combined precise finite vertex-facet incidence criterion and complete subgroup classification of every regular even-gonal plane. Dantas–del Río–Raunig introduce the underlying G-Daugavet property and give a general slice/invariant-hull characterization plus a C8 octagon example. Their stated results do not classify all dihedral subgroups, especially C_{N/2}, nor establish the exact necessary and sufficient two-step rotation threshold; the new face and subgroup arguments are substantive. Resultary returned the same submitted finding (excluded as independent predecessor) and unrelated Euclidean norm profile work, not direct coverage. There remains priority risk from implicit or unindexed polyhedral specialization.
residual_risks: General Proposition 2.9 implies this special finite criterion after a short but substantive convex-face reduction; a previously published explicit polyhedral corollary may exist under other vocabulary.
An unindexed older classification of dihedral subgroup actions on polygonal norms might cover the R² threshold.
No comprehensive historical priority or unpublished-thesis survey was possible; absence from search results is not evidence of novelty.

value.rationale: The result makes the infinitely quantified rank-one group Daugavet equation exactly decidable by a finite geometric incidence relation for every real polyhedral norm. On regular even polygons it resolves a natural minimal-group question left open by the full-rotation example: an order-N/2 cyclic subgroup is sufficient and necessary inside every qualifying dihedral subgroup, with reflections unable to substitute. This is a structural classification and exact boundary, not only a computational or renaming exercise.
residual_risks: The polyhedral reduction is fairly elementary relative to the prior general G-slice theorem, but exact all-subgroup sharpness is a nontrivial useful outcome.

limitations: The theorem is real finite-dimensional polyhedral only; regular polygons are even with N≥4.
Originality is best-of-knowledge with residual priority risk from earlier implicit/generalized geometric criteria and unindexed subgroup classifications.
